scenarios.title: Prepare an Ethernet profile for the next startup
scenarios.summary: A connection profile is a named set of saved network settings. A UUID identifies that profile; interface-name binds it to an adapter. Editing a saved file does not rewrite the settings already in use.
scenarios.objective: Prepare the saved Application profile for the next simulated startup: bind it to enp1s0, enable automatic selection and give it 10.70.0.20/24. Reach 172.16.5.10 through enp1s0, the preferred default uplink, in both supplied cases. Re-reading saved profiles must preserve the current management settings. Retain supplied filenames and UUIDs.
steps: Edit the saved virtual profiles, compare current and next-startup settings, inspect both test cases and retry.
scenarios.explanation: The worked example binds Application to enp1s0, sets autoconnect=true and repairs its supplied /24 address. Existing current selections remain snapshots; next startup uses the edited saved profile.
hints: Find the interface-name, autoconnect and address1 keys in Application; compare them with the supplied interface and task address.
A correct gateway alone cannot fix a profile bound to an absent adapter or excluded from automatic selection.
scenarios.simplifications: Bounded in-process static IPv4 Ethernet profile projection. No NetworkManager daemon, live profiles, host commands, packets or actual restart. Supported keyfiles are validated atomically; real per-file partial loading, activation failures, timestamp ties, Wi-Fi, DHCP, DNS merging, permissions and asynchronous lifecycle are not modeled. IPv6 disabled is a supplied exercise boundary, not host policy advice. Conventional interface /1–30 only; /31 and /32 remain excluded special cases. Automatic route metrics are explicit sample inputs, not universal OS defaults.

scenarios.title: Retire a stale startup preference without interrupting the current link
scenarios.summary: Only one saved Ethernet profile is selected per supplied adapter at startup. A higher autoconnect-priority is preferred. A filename or friendly name does not decide which wins.
scenarios.objective: Make the supplied Replacement profile (00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000074) win automatic selection on enp1s0 at the next startup. It must provide 10.72.0.20/24 and the usable application path to 172.16.5.10; enp1s0 remains the preferred default uplink. Re-reading files must keep BOTH current interface settings unchanged. Retain all supplied filenames and UUIDs. Do not rely on a priority tie.
steps: Edit the saved virtual profiles, compare current and next-startup settings, inspect both test cases and retry.
scenarios.explanation: The worked example raises Replacement above Old Application. Lowering the old priority or excluding the old profile from autoconnect also works. Re-reading the edited files must not replace either current selection.
hints: Compare both application profiles’ autoconnect-priority values. Higher is preferred; a tie is not a deterministic solution.
You may change eligibility or preference, while preserving the supplied UUIDs and current selections.

scenarios.title: Keep management access while changing the next default uplink
scenarios.summary: autoconnect-priority chooses a profile for one adapter. Once adapters are configured, routes choose where traffic leaves. The longest destination prefix wins; among equal-length routes, a lower route metric wins.
scenarios.objective: Prepare a two-uplink handover: at next startup enp1s0 (10.74.0.20/24) is the preferred default and reaches 172.16.5.10. Reach the management destination 10.40.0.50 through enp2s0 via its supplied gateway 10.75.0.1 in both metric contexts. Re-reading files must preserve current management settings. Retain supplied filenames and UUIDs; use supported explicit routes/metrics or never-default policy without metric ties.
steps: Edit the saved virtual profiles, compare current and next-startup settings, inspect both test cases and retry.
scenarios.explanation: The worked example gives Application an explicit metric 50, suppresses Management’s default and adds its specific 10.40.0.0/24 route. Another supported solution can retain both defaults with explicit unequal metrics and the specific management route.
hints: Separate the default destination from the specific management destination. Compare each chosen route, not only which adapters have addresses.
An explicit management route is still needed after selecting the application default. Test both supplied automatic-metric cases.
scenarios.simplifications: Bounded in-process static IPv4 Ethernet profile projection. No NetworkManager daemon, live profiles, host commands, packets or actual restart.
